joins-and-cardinality.title: Why a duplicate lookup multiplies tickets
joins-and-cardinality.summary: Each left row pairs with every matching right row. A two-row billing lookup doubles the two billing tickets.

nodes.label: Two billing tickets
nodes.description: T001 and T003 each represent one completed ticket.

nodes.label: Two billing owners
nodes.description: The lookup incorrectly contains both Asha and Sam for the same team key.

nodes.label: Four matched rows
nodes.description: Each of the two tickets pairs with each owner, producing four rows.

nodes.label: Reject many-to-one violation
nodes.description: validate="many_to_one" detects that billing is duplicated on the right. Fix the lookup before reporting.

steps.title: Inspect the input grain
steps.explanation: The left side is one row per ticket. The intended lookup should have one row per team.

steps.title: Follow every match
steps.explanation: Two tickets multiplied by two lookup records produces four output rows.

steps.title: Stop before aggregation
steps.explanation: Cardinality validation rejects the duplicate team key. Row counts alone cannot tell which owner is correct.
